item.title: The Biggest Price Spikes in Pokémon This Week - 11/18/2026
item.description:
Pokémon|finance

The Biggest Price Spikes in Pokémon This Week - 11/18/2026

You can't keep a good cat down.

By Corbin Hosler

|@Chosler
|

Published Nov 18, 2026

|

4 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series: Movers and Shakers

I know it's trendy to talk these days about how the Pokémon market is slowing down. About how some of the market is correcting, about how many more cards are printed these days, and about how there's just no future in modern Pokémon chase hits.

And then Delta Reign released, and we watched Raikou ex leap up in price.

Delta Reign Defies the Dip

Will this Raikou ex hold the $105 Market Price it has today long-term? Maybe not. But even as more Delta Reign has entered the market over the last week, we've seen the price of the Special Illustration Rare climb in price, and quite drastically. That $105 Market Price tag it carries today is way up from the $90 it was coming out of the gate last week. Clearly, there's still demand for new Pokémon cards, at least high quality Illustration Rare and Special Illustration Rare cards like Raikou.

Elsewhere in Delta Reign, things are progressing more as expected. The headliner SIR Mega Rayquaza ex is actually outpacing the gold version of the same, and both are sliding down slowly in price since release. The gold version (MHR Mega Rayquaza has predictably slid from $225 down to $210 over the last week, while the true chase of the set, Mega Rayquaza, has dipped slightly from $310 down to under $300.

On the other hand, IR Kecleon has been a bit of a surprise winner from the set, moving from $23 at its low to closer to $30+ today. It's easy to see why, given such beautiful artwork on the seldom-seen Pokémon. Similarly, Mega Golisopod ex 135 has actually inched up from $20 to $25 in that same time.

So if you were wondering whether the unlucky set that had to follow 30th Celebration would have its own share of hits, it looks like Delta Reign didn't disappoint in that regard.

Old Promos Spike Unexpectedly

Mewtwo-EX XY125 originally was available in a Super-Premium Collection, back in 2016. Since then, it's been a very slow—but very steady—climb up to its current all-time high Market Price. Once available for as low as $5, Mewtwo-EX had climbed up to $30 by the time 2025 rolled around—and then more than doubled to $75 by the start of 2026. Somehow, it's only gained steam since.

The current run on Mewtwo-EX began around the end of the summer, when the card first began to push up to the $100 threshold, only to keep going. After yet another strong first half of a month, we saw the Market Price on Mewtwo-EX XY125 push all the way up to a new all-time high of nearly $200, with live Near Mint listings stretching even beyond that.

I don't know if it was the Lugia focus from the Classic Collection in 30th Celebration that started the ball rolling on the Reverse Holofoil Lugia from 2016's Fates Collide, but it's gaining speed now. The card started the summer out at just around $5, but has been on an incredible run ever since. It first climbed up to $10 around September, and this week has begun to push even higher as copies slowly dwindle. Like many older (or in this case, mid-era) cards, the movement here is halting, but it is emblematic of where much of the market is putting its focus these days.

New Promos Predictably Drop

Speaking of cards dropping in price, the 2026 McDonald's set of cards is out and the prices are falling fast, with nothing fetching more than $5 (predictably, Pikachu takes 1st place). These limited-release runs can sometimes get pretty pricey, especially years later, so if you're trying to get a little weird with it and catch all the Pokémon you can inside a Happy Meal, you can complete the release quite easily right now.

And while we are on the subject of promos…

A futuristic Pikachu and a gorgeous piece of Espeon art featuring multiple cameos from other Pokémon? That's a slam dunk of a duo, and both of these new releases are available for an ever-more affordable price. 

As they come out of the gate and the market settles, it looks like Pikachu ex has settled around $20-$25, while Espeon ex is coming in closer to $30. With 30th Celebration product still being rolled out and promos still hitting the market, it's difficult to predict exactly where these go from here, but the price for those collecting 30th Celebration is looking quite affordable—especially compared to those $3,000 RBG Mews.

Ascended Heroes and Destined Rivals Continue to Fall

Finally, let's look at the biggest drop of 2026—coming after the climb of 2026—in Ascended Heroes. The set was full of hits and hugely hyped when it was released, and then things began to climb even higher from there. Mega Gengar ex was once pushing $1,400.

Times have changed, as mass reprints of this and other 2026 sets have absolutely cratered prices on the biggest hits in the set. There's nothing to scoff at in a $550 Mega Gengar ex, but that's down $50 in Market Price this week, and obviously worlds away from $1,400. Similarly, Pikachu ex dropped from $560 down to $520. Of course, it's all relative—these are still insanely good hits from a booster pack.

The same goes for SIR Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex from Destined Rivals, the Team Rocket-focused set that is stacked with cool designs. It also had one of several mega chase cards in Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex, but reprints have similarly brought prices down. This week Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex dropped from $310 to $280. 

Until next week, good luck pulling Rayquaza from your Delta Reign!

item.title: The Best (and Worst) Yu-Gi-Oh! Thanksgiving Dinners
item.description:
Yu-Gi-Oh!|casual

The Best (and Worst) Yu-Gi-Oh! Thanksgiving Dinners

...Maybe it's better to just stay home.

By Tyler Berger

|

Published Nov 25, 2026

|

2 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

The holiday season is upon us, and many are preparing for the annual food and family get-togethers. This can be a delightful time of year, or a stressful one, so I thought: what if we could join one of Yu-Gi-Oh's families for a Duel Monster dinner instead? Could some of these might even be an upgrade?

It's Supposed to Be Thanksgiving, Not a Wight Christmas

Surely, a holiday with royalty would be lovely, right? Perhaps not with the King of the Skull Servants and his family. First of all, I'm not even sure they'd serve dinner. While Wightbaking's sweet potatoes look pretty tasty, look at The Lady in Wight's food covered in cobwebs and spiders – I don't trust them with a proper meal. And who's to say they'd even make it to the gathering on time? Remember when they forgot that There Can Be Only One, and then got their dogs stuck in Quarantine? 

At Least It's Quiet

Family dinner in the Silent household might be a little awkward. "Hey Silent Swordsman, could you pass the gravy?" No answer. "So Silent Paladin, I heard you were starting a new job?" Nothing. "So how 'bout that local sports team, eh Silent Magician?" Like talking to a brick wall. 

On the plus side, you don't have to worry about Silent Uncle trying to talk about politics. 

Turkey Gobblin' with the Goblins

Here we go, this is the good stuff. Look at these happy goblin kids! Doing a Gift Exchange, maybe wearing Matching Outfits, that's the holiday spirit! Even if you hate the Scrap Kong t-shirt you got, these are the memories you'll cherish when you're older. 

And we haven't even gotten to the food! These goblins don't mess around, enjoying a Token Thanksgiving or saying Oh Tokenbaum! Yes, I would eat a Scapegoat. I'd eat four.

Also, I'd wear the heck out of a Scrap Kong shirt. Just saying, if any family is reading this…

While it's fun to imagine, we can't jump into the world of Duel Monsters for the holidays… for better or worse. So I wish all the readers out there a happy Thanksgiving holiday, whether it's with family, friends, or even just your pets. Maybe you don't even celebrate. What's important is that you remember what you're thankful for, like your super sweet Scrap Kong t-shirt.

item.title: The Best-Selling Cards in Disney Lorcana Right Now (November 2026)
item.description:
Disney Lorcana|collecting|finance

The Best-Selling Cards in Disney Lorcana Right Now (November 2026)

You didn't need to be a detective to see this one coming!

By Scott Mines

|@HowlingMines
|

Published Nov 25, 2026

|

8 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series: Bestselling Cards of the Week

Happy holidays, Illumineers!  

I hope that you're jammed full of turkey and playing games with the family by the time this article is hitting your eyeballs... unless you live somewhere that doesn't do Thanksgiving like me. In that case, I just hope you're not too cold.  

As I alluded to in my previous article, I'll be jamming plenty of Disney Lorcana at my own little "Friendsgiving" though. The game is in a bit of a strange place right now, with the enjoyable variety amongst top performing deck lists being blunted slightly by frustrating play experiences that feel like they've outstayed their welcome.

Regardless, Disney Lorcana Challenge: London was a blast to watch and showcased some of the best players in the world navigating their way through complicated questions and difficult boardstates. The metagame wasn't settled and was arguably upheaved by the eventual winner — Amber Sapphire Detectives, which was on the way up but not sitting at the top.  

What we didn't realize in the moment was that this result would open the floodgates. 

Detectives are cheap, thematic and absurdly competitive, which is a magical combination of factors that sends the market haywire. Since that success, multiple cards that serve as the lynchpins of that archetype have been purchased en masse each and every day. That got me curious: what does the rest of the Disney Lorcana market look like right now?  

Good question, mysterious voice in my brain. Shall we take a peek at the best-selling cards in Disney Lorcana this month?  

#10: Elisa Maza - Hardworking Detective

Introducing the first member of our illustrious detective crew: Elisa Maza - Hardworking Detective.

I've been a pretty vocal advocate that Elisa is secretly the best card in the deck. That's the kind of power that pulls an uncommon up onto a bestsellers list that's typically littered with legendaries.  

Perfect information is always the most powerful thing you can gain in any card game. Elisa Maza provides you with everything you'll need to know about the opponent's plans while tearing the most problematic non-character out of them. Even better, she's self-enabling. It's not uncommon to chain Elisa into another copy to keep the disruption coming.  

This card is an important part of making one of the best decks in the game function, which feels like a steal at twelve cents.  

#9: Don Karnage - Debonair Pirate

Tinker Bell - Giant Fairy's fresh coat of Emerald paint left us with a potent threat in Core Constructed. Don Karnage - Debonair Pirate may not have been as format warping as players guessed he would be when he released in Hyperia City, but it regularly appears as a two-of in both top Emerald decks in the format.  

I expect Don Karnage to age incredibly well, especially if a premier shift target is printed. It's the style of card to dominate in the wake of rotation and will clean your clock if you're playing something aggressive. It should continue floating in and out of the bestseller list across the next few months.  

#8: Aurora - Delightful Musician 

A top tier princess at just $2 is a rare sight in Disney Lorcana and the community is taking note. You don't get Sleeping Beauty at that price point. Heck, I don't even get sleep at that price point! 

Aurora - Delightful Musician has shown up in a variety of Amber Emerald and Amber Steel decklists focused on songs, but the latter has proven to be a more appealing home overall. The card hasn't cemented itself as a mainstay yet, but it feels like it'll age well as more songs make their way into the format.

Hyperia City has a robust song theme that I wouldn't be surprised to see fleshed out further in Into the Inkdark early next year. This seems like a snazzy investment if you enjoyed old school Steelsong in the past.

#7: Mulan - Martial Arts Master

Mulan is my steal of a pickup though. I think it's criminal that this card is only sitting at $2 when it reads like a Ruby mainstay for a long time to come.  

If you were anything like me, you may have spent the weeks before Hyperia City reveal season complaining about how all the good Ruby cards are uninkable. Mulan - Martial Arts Master answered those concerns with a character that's impactful on play and on quest.  

The card has found a reasonable about of success in the current builds of Ruby Amethyst as a half Merlin - Crab and half Madam Mim - Fox. Most other Ruby decks in the format right now revolve around Rivera Family Photo and The Torn Corner, which doesn't really suit Mulan's skillset.  

Mark my words — this card will be a monster of the format at some point. I just feel it in my bones.

#6: Merlin's Shop and Smithy - Magical Market

I think people forgot how backbreaking a cheap, high willpower location that can gain lore has the potential to be. It brings me a sick kind of joy to see Merlin's Shop and Smithy - Magical Market reminding them in style.  

This location really shines in Amber Amethyst, where it can benefit from the abundance of ink drops by funneling cheaper characters into the shop to refill your hand. It also offers a surprising amount of closing power across multiple turns. You get to seventeen lore and the victory starts to feel inevitable.  

It's not quite Merlin - Goat or The Queen's Castle - Mirror Chamber, but it doesn't need to be. Merlin's Shop and Smithy - Magical Market dips into the powerful aspects of both to create a unique beast that players are loving.  

#5: Max Goof - Karaoke Star

Mind-blowing ability? Check. A shift target to a second potent legendary? You got it. The backbone of one of the better decks in the game? Stop, I was already sold.  

Max Goof - Karaoke Star does it all. More importantly, that isn't going to change any time soon.  

Emerald Amber Circle of Life loves Max Goof. You've got situationally powerful songs like Akood et Emuti, Mean, Malicious, and Scary and To Wither a Flower that you'll happily ditch to draw yourself closer to your big combo turns when they're blank, all of which are fantastic targets for a Max Goof - Chart Topper that you shift atop of the karaoke star. It's like somebody designed a custom card shift target for the existing floodborn!  

Don't count out "Brand New Playlist" when considering this card either. I have lost an annoying number of games to a topdecked Max Goof - Karaoke Star that just happens to quest for four.  

#4: Judy Hopps - Day Camp Instructor

Finally, we're entering detective town good and proper. Judy Hopps - Day Camp Instructor doesn't quite manage to make the podium this month, but it is part of a larger buying pattern surrounding Disney Lorcana's hottest new competitor.  

Judy plays an important role in accelerating your ink early, all while deploying several must-answer characters to the board. Once that work is done, it'll be a constant inconvenience thanks to Support, which gets some of those other characters trading up for more expensive characters as the opponent plays them.  

The best part? Nobody wants to waste removal effects on Judy. If you're careful with your questing, it's not uncommon for her to lock down a board and leave the opponent unable to profitably quest. 

#3: Judy Hopps - Always Vigilant

I swear these Zootopia cards are breeding like rabbits.  

Judy Hopps - Always Vigilant is another part of why Judy Hopps - Day Camp Instructor is so potent. Once you're at four ink, it's very easy to play another character before shifting into her amber counterpart, completely sinking the first meaningful threat from your opponent. It's a nasty play pattern that deck lists are being built to respect moving forward.  

I'd hop on this one quickly, too. Judy is up 56% in the last thirty days, selling roughly 1300 copies this month. Her record high was an impressive $4.69 for a rare. If you don't have yours yet, pick them up while they're still just a dollar! 

#2: Mickey Mouse - Best in Town

The Best in Town no longer, it seems.  

Mickey has been selling strong since it was released in Hyperia City, but it previously sat almost uncontested as the most coveted card from the set. While the iconic variant still holds that title in the heavyweight division, the base variant has been usurped in the bestsellers.  

Make no mistake: everybody still wants this card. It's seeing play across a variety of Amber decks and puts the fear of God into your opponent whenever it's played on turn one. No, this is more likely to be a case of "most people that wanted them have finally picked them up".  

Forty-five copies a day is nothing to turn your nose up at though. In fact, I would take the fact that Mickey Mouse - Best in Town is trending back towards its cheapest price ever as an endorsement to snap them up if you haven't.  

#1: Nick Wilde - Toy Drive Officer

But at the end of the day, it all comes back to Amber Sapphire Detectives. 

As one of the Super Rares that the archetype needs four copies of, players were less likely to have every copy of Nick Wilde - Toy Drive Officer that they needed in their collection already. As a result, they're jumping on the marketplace to get in while the getting is good.  

This card is up an eyewatering 178% in the last thirty days and doesn't look to be slowing down. If only there was some way to have seen this inevitable success coming? Wouldn't that have been lovely?

Written By

item.title: Cause Absolute Mayhem With Star Trek's Q, Stacking the Deck in Commander
item.description:
Magic: The Gathering|Commander|casual

Cause Absolute Mayhem With Star Trek's Q, Stacking the Deck in Commander

He has no powers! He's just ordinary.

By Jason Coles

|

Published Nov 25, 2026

|

4 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series: Commander Bestiary

Magic: The Gathering | Star Trek is bringing with it all sorts of goodies for Commander players. That not only includes some exceptional reprints in the preconstructed Commander decks, but also some intriguing mechanical options from the main set itself. From among those, one has proven to be the most popular by a fair margin, and we're going to get into it in this guide about everything Q, Stacking the Deck.

Our Commander Bestiary series is all about ensuring you leave each article with some exciting new ideas. We cover not only some information about the character, but also the strengths and weaknesses of the card, and even some combos. That's the low-down, so let's get the high-up on everything now. 

A Simple Name (for a Complicated Being)

Q is a singular being from a race also called Q. He's essentially a pseudo-god, with powers that can disrupt and alter time, space, and basically anything else they feel like. They're a bit of a trickster more than anything else, and they tend to use all of that power to keep things entertaining while also silently judging humanity as a whole. You can also call Q at (323) 634–5667 thanks to an episode of Star Trek: Picard.

As for the Magic card, Q, Stacking the Deck is a four-mana red 4/4 that reads, "When Q enters, shuffle your library, then exile cards from the top of your library until you exile a nonland card. That nonland card gains "Exile a card from your hand: Create a copy of this card. You may cast the copy. Activate only during your turn and only if this card is exiled." In short, you exile cards from your library until you hit a nonland card, then you can cast a copy of it during your turn by exiling a card from your hand and paying the mana cost as you normally would. There are a bunch of very silly combos you can do with this, like having only one nonland card in the deck, but there's also an opportunity to lean into the chaos of it all. It's genuinely an interesting and fun strategy to play.

Q comes with zero protection, but it's also largely irrelevant once he's entered the battlefield. The card gains the ability without Q, meaning it being removed leads to you having more options if you decide to cast him again. It's hard to control Q's ability unless you're building a specific kind of combo deck, so expect a lot of variance in your games. Q fits best in any mono-red strategy, whether that's burn, aggro, or chaos, but it does especially well when you're getting benefits for casting things from exile. You can also stack your deck, pun intended, with cards like Glaring Fleshraker. Then, simply copy effects and ping everyone to death. The choices are endless, the options are infinite, and being silly is a priority.

Definitely Stacking the Deck (For the Win, That Is)

Mono-red is incredibly good at going infinite with various enter the battlefield triggers. A classic example of this is Molten Duplication and Dualcaster Mage. You need both of these in hand, and at least one creature in play. From there, you cast the Duplication, then before it resolves, cast the Dualcaster to copy it, you can then use that copied spell to target the Dualcaster Mage, and just keep going forever. You can win comfortably with this by using something like Impact Tremors to deal damage to everyone. 

How To Play Q, Stacking the Deck in Commander

For our picks here, we're mostly focused on benefiting from Q's ability to exile cards and then cast them from exile. First up on our list of cards that are quite good here is Delayed Blast Fireball. This is a three-mana instant that deals two damage to each opponent and creature they control unless you cast it from exile, in which case it's five-mana. That's an impressive boost, and it makes for a fantastic board wipe.

Dragon's Smile is a seven-mana 4/5 vehicle with flying and a crew cost of 3. During your turns, you can pay 0 to cast a card from exile, but only once. That's already absolutely huge, but it can also exile some cards from your library when it deals combat damage to someone. Spider-Verse is a five-mana enchantment which allows you to copy spells you cast from exile once per turn too. With both cards in play you'll get a free card that then doubles itself. If you're doing that with Delayed Blast Fireball, that's ten damage to everyone else and their creatures for no mana spent.

You want more value though, and I get that. So, add Wild-Magic Sorcerer to the deck. This four-mana 4/3 gives the first spell you cast from exile each turn cascade, allowing you to cast even more spells. Finally, we've got Conjurer's Closet, a five-mana artifact that lets you blink a creature you control in your end step. Even if the only target for this in your entire deck is Q, Stacking the Deck, that offers a lot of value, and a great way of getting more options to cast from exile too.

All of these make for a fantastic deck that gives a lot of value for each card. Keep in mind that if you do get any of these in exile, you can keep casting them all game long without Q in play. It's a fantastic interaction, and something that feels a fair bit different to a lot of other commanders.

item.title: Everything We Know About Magic: The Gathering's Nauctis: The Sunken Realm Set
item.description:
Magic: The Gathering|casual|competitive|news

Everything We Know About Magic: The Gathering's Nauctis: The Sunken Realm Set

Breaching the depths of Magic collectibility.

By Jason Coles

|

Published Nov 26, 2026

|

6 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

2027 might be a slightly calmer year for Magic: The Gathering in terms of set releases, but I don't think it'll be less exciting. The first set of the year is Nauctis: The Sunken Realm, and it's an in-universe one as well. That means there's a chance for Planeswalkers alongside some new advances in the story. It'll be interesting to see what that looks like now that Jace has echo'd all over the place.

Everything We Know About Magic: The Gathering's Nauctis: The Sunken Realm Set

Nauctis: The Sunken Realm is going to be Standard-legal, so you'll be able to use the cards from the core set in any format. Thematically, Nauctis is all about water and the creatures that live in it. Some are cute, and some are less cute – or at least more niche in their cuteness. Either way though, I want to make sure you have the lowdown, so here's everything you need to know about Nauctis: The Sunken Realm. 

Nauctis: The Sunken Realm Key Dates and Events

Nauctis: The Sunken Realm is going to be in everyone's hands as of February 5, 2027. I really like the fact that nothing is actually released in January for a change, even though we'll be getting plenty of previews in the two weeks prior to the actual release, if not a little longer to make sure that 2027 starts off strong.

  • Prerelease Events: January 29–February 4
  • Magic Presents: Black History Month Celebration: February 1–28
  • MTG Arena and Magic Online Release Date: February 2
  • Tabletop Release: February 5
  • Store Championship: February 19–March 18
  • MagicCon: Detroit and Pro Tour Nauctis: February 26–28
  • Nauctis: The Sunken Realm Set Code: NAU
  • Commander: Nauctis: The Sunken Realm Set Code: NAC
  • Special Guests Set Code: SPG

I'd expect previews to end around January 22 based on how these things tend to go, but it could be a few days before or after it, depending on how Wizards of the Coast decides to plan things next year. There'll be plenty of things to look for, and a mass of new sea critters to build around, both little cute ones and the massive unsettling ones too. 

Standard Constructed Rotation With Nauctis: The Sunken Realm

If you're someone who's playing Standard, it's worth mentioning that Standard rotation will trigger upon Nauctis' Prerelease weekend on January 29. The sets rotating out will be:

  • Wilds of Eldraine (WOE)
  • The Lost Caverns of Ixalan (LCI)
  • Murders at Karlov Manor (MKM)
  • Outlaws of Thunder Junction (OTJ)
  • Bloomburrow (BLB)
  • Duskmourn: House of Horror (DSK)

This means cards from the above sets won't be eligible to play in Standard upon Nauctis' release, unless they've been reprinted in sets since then or via Magic Foundations. Losing out on value and playability isn't always ideal, but Pioneer will be making a return in April and will be part of the Regional Qualifiers for that period. This means your cards may go a little further, especially if you're someone vying for a Pro Tour invitation. Wizards recently announced the schedule, and you can read more about it right here.

Nauctis: The Sunken Realm Mechanics 

It's early days at the moment, but it's clear from the cards we saw at MagicCon Atlanta that there will be a lot of discarding cards, sacrificing cards, and a focus on the graveyard as well. The return of blood tokens is a little bit surprising, but does feel fitting given that there are sharks like Goramou the Coral-Taken swimming around waiting to strike. It looks like there'll be some truly titanic creatures as well, with Tecton, Malignant Ruin and Salinae, the Ocean Mother both costing eight mana normally, although they both get cheaper based on the permanents in your graveyard or your devotion to blue respectively.

It also looks like artifacts could play a big role too. Blood tokens hint at that, but so does the headliner card this time around: Abyssal Lotus. This brand-new lotus still costs 0 to cast, but only gives you three mana if you've got eight or more permanents in your graveyard. It's quite possible we'll see some new self-mill cards and payoffs as well in Nauctis. We're going to have to wait and see what else is coming though. 

Nauctis: The Sunken Realm Products

We're getting Booster Packs (formerly called Play Boosters) and Collector Boosters as always, although they come with a fun new wrinkle. One in one-thousand Booster Packs will be a God Pack, which contains only rare and mythic rare cards, with the same applying to Collector Boosters in around one in three-hundred packs. The excitement of opening one of those is sure to encourage more boosters sales than usual, so keep your fingers crossed, and we hope you get lucky on that front.

We're getting a normal Bundle for this set, and we're also getting a Secret Lair Bundle as well. The Secret Lair one is unusual, and it'll have six Booster Packs, two Collector Boosters, and two traditional foil Secret Lair promo cards, and some foil full-art basic lands as well. Then there's the return of the Draft Night Box for friends who love limited, and of course, Prerelease Packs too.

We're also getting four brand-new Commander Decks, each of which has a standard and a Premium Edition. While you might wonder why these aren't sharing the "Collector's Edition" naming as seen with Universes Beyond releases, this is because Premium Edition means every card in the box is traditional foil (instead of being surge foil).

Merfolk Regiment is a green, white, and blue deck all about merfolk and going wide. Terrors of the Abyss is a black, green, and white deck about discard, mill, and reanimating massive sea monsters. Blood in the Water is a blue and red shark-based deck built to attack and make the most of what Blood tokens can do (Jaws reprint one time, please). The final one is obviously the best though: Seal the Deal is a red and white Group Hug deck about trading and amassing Treasure. Group Hug decks are still evil, but we'll suffer through a lot more for an adorable seal. 

Nauctis: The Sunken Realm Art Treatments

Another set means yet more stunning art treatments. The chase card and headliner this time is the Abyssal Lotus. There'll be approximately 500 of this card available to collect, and it does look absolutely stunning as a raised foil and with the art they've chosen for it. If you get this one, that'll probably use all of your luck for 2027. Box toppers will now come in a pearlescent foil or an undersea foil. The only card we've seen for those is Crucible of Worlds, but there will be 15 reprints available and five brand-new cards to collect as well.

The Ocean Panorama cards are borderless and feature one of 24 different options, and are also designed with flavor text unique to the cards to help tie the whole thing together. Having special flavor text is a really interesting move, and gives just a little bit more of a reason to actually try and go for these. The final unique option is the Coral Frame cards, which there are 28 of. These look a bit like the Sculptor's Stronghold cards from Reality Fracture, and I hope that's a theme that continues as it'll make for some very pretty decks if so.

Finally, we're getting borderless lands, Japan showcase cards, and the Secret Lair Bundle cards too. So, as ever, there are plenty of very pretty cards to try to collect, if you're looking to do so. That's it for now though, at least until we get more information on this rather wet set.

item.title: The Best-Selling Cards in Flesh and Blood Right Now (November 2026)
item.description:
Flesh and Blood|collecting|finance

The Best-Selling Cards in Flesh and Blood Right Now (November 2026)

Assassins, Ice and... Garbage?

By Scott Mines

|@HowlingMines
|

Published Nov 26, 2026

|

8 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series: Bestselling Cards of the Week

I'm hopeful that you'll be passed out in some kind of turkey-fueled food coma by the time you're reading this article. If you're also foolish enough to be in a country that doesn't celebrate Thanksgiving, may I suggest purchasing some sealed product to make the day a little brighter? That's my excuse and I'm sticking with it.  

Apparently, I'm not the only one. Flesh and Blood has had one of its strongest months on the TCGplayer marketplace in recent memory throughout November, primarily off the back of the hotly anticipated Mastery Pack: Assassin and events that transpired at the World Championship. We didn't just learn which decks currently stand atop the competitive landscape; we learned details about almost every release for the next twelve months.  

That fuels speculation and excitement — both of which are great for business.  

It helps that Mastery Pack: Assassin has stuck the landing. Uzuri, Switchblade has been revitalized, Arakni, Huntsman has evolved into a tyrant of the metagame, and Dr. Mortimer, Blight of the Pits is cutting his teeth as a viable way to attack popular strategies. Players are clamoring to get their hands on these cards as these heroes continue to blossom, and collectors are loving the premium treatments that they're able to find inside the packs.

Add in a sprinkle of speculation and some breakout decks from the last few weekends? Suddenly, we find ourselves with a spicy bestsellers list at the end of the month. Shall we take a closer look at the best-selling cards in Flesh and Blood during November?  

#10: Frost Hex

See, you all get it. There's only one queen of our hearts for all things FAB, and her name is Iyslander.  

I could let my heat of the moment tweet do the talking here, but I'm paid to be more articulate than that. During the World Championship keynote, the much-beloved Iyslander was confirmed to be returning to the game after an almost three-year hiatus as a part of Q3's Ancients Awaken. Unsurprisingly, diehards like me lost our collective minds.  

Frost Hex is one of the more memorable specializations in Flesh and Blood, both because the effect is unique and it comes in Cold Foil. It previously featured as a stunning endgame combo piece with Insidious Chill, Amulet of Ice and Ice Eternal: a play pattern that Ice Wizard enjoyers are eager to see return.  

I've held onto my Cold Foil copies all this time because I'm a sentimental soul. If you didn't, it makes sense to grab them now.  

#9: Tailored Targeting

I have a horrible feeling that I'm going to detest this card in a couple of months.

Tailored Targeting may as well be a custom card for Arakni, Huntsman. The card would be threatening enough in its own right, but it also interacts profitably with Flick Knives and Graven Call to banish up to four cards from the opposing deck each time at almost zero cost.  

Arakni was previously flush with 0-for-4 contract cards that didn't excite you but served an important role in proactively fatiguing the opposing deck and generating Silver tokens. In the wake of Mastery Pack: Assassin, you can be far pickier in your deckbuilding now.  

If you're playing Arakni, Huntsman, you'll want three Tailored Targeting. It's that simple.  

#8: Looking for a Scrap (Blue)

Thomas Bailey Galbraith did a number on the collective psyche of the Flesh and Blood community when he managed to make the Top 8 of Calling: Sydney with a highly innovative variant of Viserai, the Forsaken that revolves around Looking for a Scrap. The deck contains the full nine copies and drew plenty of attention after an undefeated day one.  

Looking for a Scrap allows you to banish a Bloodfrenzy Gloomblade or Demonbound Gloomblade from your graveyard, which can then be played from the banish zone for efficient numbers and an active Seven Sin Nebula. The blue and yellow variants of the card have seen a collective zero play prior to this deck, which left everyone hunting copies if they intended to play it.  

It's unclear if the deck continues to perform, but I'm willing to find out for twenty cents a copy.  

#7: Demoralize the Dracai

At a glance, Demoralize the Dracai reads like a less exciting version of Excessive Bloodloss, which is pretty disappointing for a signpost majestic from a Mastery Pack. Upon further inspection, it really does point in the direction that Dr. Mortimer, Blight of the Pits is supposed to be built.  

If you take an aggressive stance with Dr. Mortimer's hero ability, Demoralize the Dracai can threaten to generate Silver across multiple chain links. This quickly refunds the Silver you spent to give Demoralize the Dracai Go Again in the first place.  

In my eyes, the card clearly shines as one of the better one-cost contracts, and I'm expecting it to become a mainstay in deck lists for our new medical professional. It plays much better than it reads.  

#6: Mutually Assured Destruction

I'm surprised to see this card placing so highly, but it's definitely proven itself to be a wrecking ball against opponents who rely on defense reactions to keep your threats in check. There's plenty of those lurking across the metagame right now.  

Mutually Assured Destruction will have you spraying Bloodrot Pox all over the place, enabling everything from Cadaver Handlers to Sick Intent while forcing the opponent to bleed out. It'll even allow Dr. Mortimer to make some Silver in a pinch if you need to.  

It's important to remember that you don't often care much about taking some damage to a Bloodrot Pox yourself when your goal is to force damage through against a defensive opponent. Mutually Assured Destruction really shines in that style of matchup and often ends up in the sideboard when it's all about the race.  

#5: Looking for a Scrap (Yellow)

Why did we sell slightly more yellow copies than blue ones? I couldn't tell you. I guess people were more likely to have had blue copies previously for Kayo, Underhanded Cheat or something?  

There's not a lot I can say about this one that I didn't cover in its blue counterpart above. Turns out people are in love with their garbage lately, and it's all thanks to Viserai, the Forsaken.  

#4: Remember the Mists

You'll find all four of our best-selling cards this month woven into my upgrade guide for Dr. Mortimer, Blight of the Pits and thus can find more details about their powers over there. That said, it's got me feeling happy that I've guided people in the right direction!  

Remember the Mists was honestly the card I expected to sit on the throne this month with how ubiquitous it is. It's not quite Surgical Extraction, but it still threatens to rip away important cards from the opposing hand. It's a blue attack that blocks three with a breakpoint. It just does a bit of everything.  

I expect the card to continue to trend upwards, especially if Uzuri, Switchblade shows up at Calling: Shenzhen or Calling: Wakefield.  

#3: Outbreak

Get it? They named it after the next upcoming booster set because it's going to be absurd in those heroes as well! Outbreak is a hammer that you'll need to respect out of every assassin resource base moving forward, threatening disease and disruption wherever it goes.  

While Dr. Mortimer may benefit from the diseases the most, every assassin can score five or more value from this blue reaction. That's an incredible rate that's easy to pitch stack as you navigate your way through the early turns.  

I expect Outbreak to be a mainstay of the class for a long time, so I'd encourage you to snap up some copies if you intend to get stabbin'  

#2: Expense Not Spared

While I still don't think this card is as heinous as the internet would have you believe on reveal, Expense Not Spared is turning out to be a matchup-defining card in several cases. +5 is a hefty bonus by itself, but it's particularly gnarly when combined with many of assassin's premier on-hit effects

Leave No Witnesses and friends get very scary in the second cycle once this card is nearly always online, but the standout performer to me has been Eradicate. If you're able to pitch stack 14+ power Eradicates in the endgame, you'll clean up those defense opponents.  

It's also a headache for Gravy Bones, Shipwrecked Looter, who will give you a chunk of Silver as his allies disappear into the banished zone.  

#1: Sick Intent

Sick Intent is unquestionably the breakout majestic from Mastery Pack: Assassin, appearing in every legal assassin in some number. At worst, it threatens to be a two-card eight that'll make you a Silver. At best? It'll obliterate your opponent with Cadaver Handlers, Spreading Plague and a selection of other ways to make diseases as an instant.  

I think this card is still underpriced at twenty bucks. The more I play with it, the more backbreaking it feels. It's an unshakable three-of for both Dr. Mortimer and Uzuri, and should appear in moderation for both Arakni, Huntsman and Slippy. If any of the heroes from Outbreak want it? I can see Sick Intent getting expensive pretty fast.

item.title: The Ultimate Black Friday Gift Guide for Pokémon TCG Fans in 2026
item.description:
Pokémon

The Ultimate Black Friday Gift Guide for Pokémon TCG Fans in 2026

When they say they want Pokémon cards, here's what they mean.

By Peter Day

|

Published Nov 20, 2026

|

6 min read

Copy Link
TCGplayer Series:

The holidays are right around the corner! If you're hoping to surprise and delight a certain Pokémon Trainer in your life, you've come to the right place. We have traveled across the land (searching far and wide) to discover the perfect present for every type of Poké Fan.

Buying brand-new sealed Pokémon card products hasn't been easy in 2026. For the past two years, a boom in Pokémon card collecting has led to shortages of sealed product all over the world. While The Pokémon Company International has been reprinting waves of product to meet the demand, and card prices have come down as a result, many sealed products have remained stubbornly hard to find at MSRP.

It's not all doom and gloom, though! A few underrated gems are still totally affordable, and given how hard it's been to find great deals this year, your Pokémon Trainer will appreciate you putting in the legwork for them all the more.

These are the best holiday gifts for players and collectors of the Pokémon TCG in 2026.

Best Stocking Stuffer: Booster Pack

They like Pokémon cards? Get them a pack of Pokémon cards! Every Pokémon booster pack is basically a present already, with a delightfully rippable wrapper and unknown treasures inside.

The booster pack that Pokémon fans want to open this year the most is 30th Celebration, with Ascended Heroes as a close runner-up. Both of these sets contain huge hits that have dominated social media coverage in 2026.

Ascended Heroes has SIR Mega Gengar ex and "Treekachu," while 30th Celebration has the four-figure RGB Mew cards, plus 30th anniversary reprints of Lugia from Aquapolis and Base Set Charizard. 30th Celebration also boasts the best pull rates of any set in 2026, so the odds are higher that your recipient will pull something incredible.

Unfortunately, booster packs of 30th Celebration and Ascended Heroes are priced to match their hype. Plus, they aren't sold individually at retail (though you can get them on marketplaces like TCGplayer).

If either of those facts is a deal-breaker, we'd recommend Delta Reign instead. Not only is this the newest Pokémon set released so far (and the final set of 2026), but it's got the biggest hit of 2026 outside of 30th Celebration and Ascended Heroes: SIR Mega Rayquaza ex.

You can consider Perfect Order, Chaos Rising, and Pitch Black if you know your loved one is hunting a specific card from those sets. If not, Delta Reign will be the safest choice.

Best Gift Under $30: 30th Celebration Poster Collection

If this were a normal year, we'd be recommending the 30th Celebration Booster Bundle, which retails at an MSRP of $26.94. Unfortunately, in 2026 you aren't likely to find that product for less than $60 unless you get very lucky by visiting a major retailer right as it's restocking.

Instead, at this price point we'd recommend getting the 30th Celebration Poster Collection. This collection comes with three packs, any of which might contain an RGB Mew, plus three guaranteed promo cards of three Legendary Birds, and a poster with art from the set.

30th Celebration products have been elusive all year, and any Pokémon fan would jump at a chance to try their luck with the most tantalizing packs of 2026.

Best Gift for Collectors: 30th Celebration ETB

This year, the most sure-fire gift you can give a Pokémon TCG Collector without spending hundreds of dollars is a 30th Celebration Elite Trainer Box.

Elite Trainer Boxes (ETBs) are often considered the "default" Pokémon TCG product due to their price point and how fun they are to open. Each ETB comes with nine packs, a promo card, and loads of goodies. The boxes themselves are sturdy, and fans love them for card storage and display.

Many Pokémon TCG collectors try to get a Elite Trainer Box at every set release. Because 30th Celebration ETBs were so hard to find in person and expensive to buy online when they first came out, many fans had to put this dream on hold. Receiving it as a gift will feel like all those months spent longing are finally being rewarded.

There are arguably better Pokémon products near this price point. A Delta Reign Booster Box offers far more packs per dollar. The 30th Celebration Ditto Premium Collection comes with an acrylic card display that I personally prefer over any of the goodies in an ETB.

But the sheer quantity of stuff in an ETB, and its stature in the community, make it the most gift-y-feeling option.

Best Gift for New Players: Mega Lucario ex League Battle Deck

In previous years, it was easy to recommend that new Trainers pick up a copy of the most recent Pokémon TCG Battle Academy if they wanted to learn how to play the Pokémon TCG. Unfortunately, there hasn't been a new Battle Academy since 2024, and those boxes are way more expensive than a tutorial product should be.

For now, there are no Pokémon TCG products we can recommend to brand-new players. Instead, we'd recommend that new Trainers who can read on their own learn to play with the official Pokémon TCG Live app. It's 100% free (with no in-app purchases).

Once they know how to play, if your Trainer wants to face off against friends and strangers at a school club or game store, we recommend buying them a battle deck—specifically a League Battle Deck. These "Play Level 3" preconstructed decks come with a complete 60-card deck, and they're extremely powerful right out of the box.

The deck that won the 2023 Pokémon World Championships had 39 cards in common with the Mew VMAX League Battle Deck!

This year, the League Battle Deck we most recommend is built around Mega Lucario ex, a hard-hitting attacker with a few major tournament finishes to its name. Most of the cards inside (including Mega Lucario ex itself) will be legal through 2027.

The non-"League" battle decks like the Umbreon ex and Espeon ex Battle Deck don't offer near as much power, but if one of them features your Trainer's favorite Pokémon, it will still be fun to play. It's just not likely to win a tournament.

Best Gift for the Trainer Who Has Everything

So you're shopping for a certified Poké Maniac. How can you knock their Wooloo fleece socks off them this year?

Every year around November, The Pokémon Company International releases a new Ultra-Premium Collection (UPC) designed to be the must-have gift of the season. This year, that UPC comes in two versions, based on the promos and the theme of the accessories inside.

Inside the Day or Night 30th Celebration Ultra-Premium Collection (UPC), Pokémon collectors will find a whopping 29 booster packs of the most exciting set of 2026. They'll also find two foil promo cards, a small mountain of goodies, and a bonus booster pack exclusive to these products with three cards from the 30th Celebration Classic Collection.

If money is no object and you just want to watch your favorite Trainer's jaw drop lower than it's ever dropped before, look no further. The 30th Celebration UPCs are the most coveted Pokémon TCG product you can buy in 2026.
